_doc: PRE-REGISTRATION for a candidate entry_cross_buffer reduction, filed BEFORE the runner per OP-16 (git-provable: this commit predates the replay script's own commit). Downstream of analysis/deep-research/ENTRY-EXECUTION-COST-2026-08-02.md's measurement, which found: (a) entry_cross_buffer=$0.03 is a bare code default (params.get('entry_cross_buffer', 0.03)), never once set in automation/state/params.json, aggressive/params.json, or any fleet arm's accounts.json params_patch -- unratified, unexamined, un-A/B'd since the day it shipped (2026-06-30); (b) it costs a real, mechanical $1,422 across 105 real filled entries over the measured window (3.0 cents/contract, every single row, by construction); (c) TP1/stop are computed off `mid` (heartbeat_core.py line ~2004-2005, fleet_live.py line ~449-455), NOT off `entry_px` -- so a buffer change does not alter which trades are taken, their qty, or their exit rules, making this the cleanest, lowest-blast-radius lever the measurement surfaced (distinct from -- and NOT contradicting -- the T3 entry-matrix study's STOP-A finding against a full passive-limit-below-signal redesign, analysis/recommendations/entry-exit-matrix-t3-entries.md, which tested a fundamentally different mechanism with real fill-rate risk).

hypothesis.H1_buffer_is_costly: entry_cross_buffer=$0.03 is a pure, mechanical, deterministic tax with no offsetting benefit (TP/stop are computed off mid, not entry_px, so a smaller buffer is a per-filled-trade cost-basis shift with zero interaction with exit management). Reducing it to $0.01-0.02 should show a POSITIVE aggregate P&L delta on the 105-trade real-fill population, PROVIDED fill rate survives -- fill_price <= ask_decision + candidate_buffer for the overwhelming majority of rows, since these are marketable orders and realized execution price empirically clusters below the offered limit already (avg_price_improvement_cents_per_contract = 4.11 in the parent measurement, i.e. fills already beat entry_px by more than the buffer itself, on average).
hypothesis.H2_buffer_is_load_bearing: Some trades' realized fill_price sits close enough to ask_decision+0.03 that a smaller buffer would have caused a genuine miss -- especially among the 10 real runner-cohort winners in the priced population -- and those misses erase enough of H1's savings to fail the runner-cohort zero-tolerance gate or the day-majority gate. A too-aggressive candidate (0.01) is expected to be more likely to trip H2 than a conservative one (0.02).

method.population: The 105 real filled entries scored by backtest/tools/entry_execution_cost_2026_08_02.py (analysis/recommendations/entry-execution-cost-2026-08-02.json) -- both core (safe-2/bold-2) and fleet (safe-1/safe-3/risky-1/risky-3) lanes, all 6 arms, 17 real trading days (2026-07-01..2026-07-31; the marketable-limit-plus-buffer mechanism itself did not exist before 2026-06-30, so there is no earlier population this candidate could apply to).
method.still_fills_test: fill_price <= ask_decision + candidate_buffer. DISCLOSED ASSUMPTION: realized execution price is treated as buffer-independent as long as the tighter limit still clears it -- a standard limit-order-microstructure assumption (the limit is a ceiling, not a target), NOT independently verified against Alpaca's specific price-improvement/routing internals for options. If this assumption is wrong in either direction the true effect could differ from what this replay reports; this is the single largest source of model uncertainty in this test and is disclosed as such in the write-up, not hidden.
method.filled_row_delta: delta_pnl = (0.03 - candidate_buffer) * qty * 100, added identically to EVERY trades.csv leg sharing that entry's order_id (TP1 and runner legs shift by the same per-contract amount -- they share one cost basis).
method.missed_row_delta: delta_pnl = -(sum of that entry's real realized dollar_pnl across all legs) -- the ENTIRE trade is modeled as foregone, per the mission's explicit instruction that a non-crossing limit is a missed trade, not a free option. No synthetic backfill price is substituted.
method.day_aggregation: Group by date_et (17 real trading days) for the day-majority and drop-best gates.

gates: PRIMARY: aggregate delta_pnl over all 17 available trading days (the full window since the mechanism shipped -- disclosed as short of a 25-day target, not by choice but by real-fill-history availability) must be POSITIVE.
day-majority: delta_pnl >= 0 on a majority (>= 9 of 17) of trading days.
drop-best: exclude the single best-delta trading day; aggregate over the remaining 16 must still be POSITIVE.

runner-cohort no-regression at ZERO tolerance: NONE of the 10 real runner-cohort entries (TP1 + trail/runner_target legs) in the priced population may flip from filled to missed under the candidate. Applied to ALL 10 regardless of sign -- converting a real trade into "never happened" is a participation loss even if, in some other row, it would have been a losing trade.

FILL-RATE FLOOR (first-class, not a footnote): report exact % of the 105 entries that would still cross at each candidate buffer, and the count/identity of every miss, including its foregone real P&L.
pre_registration.kill_criterion: Any gate failing on a given candidate kills that candidate outright -- no band-moving, no re-running with a friendlier threshold. If every candidate fails, entry_cross_buffer stays 0.03 and this ships as a documented null, same standing as the sibling min-entry-premium-2026-07-31.json KEEP verdict.
pre_registration.not_in_scope: This test does NOT touch min_entry_premium (reused from analysis/recommendations/min-entry-premium-2026-07-31.json, untouched), does NOT test a passive-limit-below-mid redesign (already STOP-A'd by T3 against the live exit shape), and does NOT change qty/sizing/exit rules (mechanically impossible for a buffer-only change, since those read `mid`, not `entry_px`).
